To: lindqvist-family-blog
Replying to: none
Cc: none
Subject: So, I started a business!!

Hi family!! I have some news and I wanted to tell you all before Thanksgiving, partly because I’m excited and partly because I would like to eat Aunt Ruthie’s turkey without Dad giving me a health insurance presentation in front of the entire dining room.

I started my own photography business. It’s called Fernhollow Photo and it is REAL. There is an LLC and a website and everything. I keep saying “my business” out loud to see if it sounds normal yet. It does not, but I’m working on it.

First things first: Dad, I have health insurance. I picked a marketplace plan and it starts January 1. Please put your speech away. I love you.

The short version of how we got here is that Rosebud Lane closed at the end of October. Marisol told me on October 6, and after four years of shooting for her, it was a lot to take in. I’m going to miss being part of the studio.

I also need to say something about Marisol, because I wouldn’t be doing any of this without her. She basically taught me everything. She trusted me with people’s wedding days, let me learn alongside her, and somehow made it look easy to be calm while seventeen things were happening at once. I know now that it is not easy!! She’s been in my corner from the start, and when she told me about the studio closing, she also told me she thought I was ready to do this. I cried a little then too. Apparently that’s a theme.

This wasn’t exactly how I pictured making the jump, but I’ve been planning it in my head for two years. I’ve thought a lot about what I’d want my own business to be, the kind of work I want to make, and how to take care of the people who trust me with their weddings. So yes, this is scary. Going out on my own is a big change. But I’m not just throwing a camera in the car and hoping for the best.

I already have 14 weddings booked for 2027!! Six couples came to me through Marisol, who was kind enough to refer them, and eight found me on my own. Seeing those names on my calendar makes me want to do a little dance and then immediately check the calendar again to make sure I didn’t imagine them.

For the big weddings, Jae will be second shooting with me, paid per wedding. Having another photographer there means we can be in two places at once, which is useful when one person is getting ready upstairs and the other is somehow already outside losing a boutonniere. Jae is great and I’m really glad we get to work together.

My first booking that was 100% mine was Dahlia and Ken, June 12 at Timberline. They found me because of the pictures I took of a couple at Multnomah Falls, and when they said they wanted me for their wedding I just sat there staring at the message for a minute. Somebody saw my pictures and thought, yes, we want HER. I still get a little emotional about it. Don’t tell anybody, I’m a professional.

The official LLC filing happened on my lunch break in the car outside a Fred Meyer. Very glamorous beginning for Fernhollow Photo LLC. I hit submit and cried a little in the parking lot, probably while somebody next to me was loading groceries. Then I had to pull myself together and go back to work like I hadn’t just done a thing I’d been thinking about for two years.

Sam made a cake to celebrate, which was very sweet and also said FERNHOLOW. One L short, but honestly that made it better. We ate it anyway. It turns out cake does not care how you spell the business name.

And Grandma, the name is for you. Fernhollow comes from the fern hollow trail behind your old place in Gresham, where I took my first real pictures with your Pentax. I can still picture being back there with that camera and looking at everything a little differently because I wanted to take a picture of it. It felt right to name this after the place where that started. I hope you like it. I love you.

I know some of you are probably going to have questions, and that’s okay. I’m excited and nervous at the same time, but I do have a plan. There’s work on the calendar, insurance is sorted, and I get to keep doing the thing I love. I wanted you to hear it from me because you’ve all been cheering me on for a long time, through the long weekends and sore knees and approximately a million pictures.

Also, if anyone wants free family pictures at Thanksgiving, let me know! I’ll bring the camera. We can do them before dinner so nobody has to stand outside while the turkey gets cold. Uncle Greg, I will try not to make you “freeze” again, but I’m making no promises about how long it takes us to get everybody looking in the same direction.

Love you guys. See you at Ruthie’s!!
